description.en: Build clean pulling, pushing, leg strength, trunk control, mobility, and resilient joints.
Develop pull-over control, high pulls, support strength, and assisted transitions.
Build controlled muscle-up transitions, tuck-lever foundations and supported handstand practice.
Repeat clean supported skills, strengthen tuck shapes and develop balanced full-body strength.
Develop shortened-lever strength, controlled muscle-up practice and wall-supported balance.
Consolidate strong basics and explore handstand, flag, lever and planche variations at your current ability. Use regressions freely; there is no mastery deadline.

authentic_description.en: Start with the warm-up, practise the strength sequence at a controllable difficulty, then finish with the cooldown.

catalog_notice.en: Replacement and extension sessions are newly authored and are not recovered Street Gymnastic PRO data. The app uses a balanced six-level sequence of 100 assigned workouts per level.

progression_readiness.en: Advance a movement only after you can complete its current variation with controlled range and reserve effort on at least two separate sessions. Change only one variable: repetitions, hold time, assistance or lever length. A new workout number is not a skill-readiness test; keep using an easier variation as long as needed. Later planche, straddle and full-lever shapes are practice ceilings, not requirements: use the listed regression for as long as needed.

training_recovery.en: Follow the assigned morning class, including its easy recovery sessions. Daily practice does not mean daily hard effort. If soreness or fatigue makes the warm-up unusually heavy, make today an easy walk and mobility morning, then return to the assigned strength session when recovered.

authentic_scaling.en: The morning version limits strength plus skill practice to 20 sets, with at most 3 sets per exercise, 12 repetitions or 30 seconds per hold. Former max sets are capped at 8 quality repetitions. These are ceilings: stop sooner with 2-3 repetitions in reserve and keep effort at RPE 6 in Foundations and 7 in later levels, or below. Use foot-assisted hangs and pulls, higher rows, incline push-ups, assisted dips or bent-knee raises when needed. Skip behind-the-neck pulls and head bangers. Inversions and turnovers require controlled entries, exits and suitable assistance. Recovery mornings are already assigned.
